svg.title: 11 · Presence, privacy first: counts are kept, people are not
svg.text: 11 · Presence, privacy first: counts are kept, people are not
Use case: the session sees what the bot reads, what it drops, what it keeps and for how long; an attendee hides their activity from the hub or Discord (#122, tenants.md Privacy).
· a server bound to no event
· names of people with no platform
Who plays which game, who is in which public room.
No history; replaced on every change; gone when the
event is archived. Read through the bot's API only.
Per minute: online, idle, in voice; per game: players.
Folded per hour: averages, peaks, player-hours per game.
No user ids, no names: anonymous event statistics,
kept with the event; survive a restart.
The hub's and the screens' “now playing” names (members
bot.presence.counted → the screens' numbers and graph
bot.activities.counted → Games: matching, surges, hot game
Who stayed in a match's voice
channels and how long: per person,
for one match; sent once as
Retention: nothing raw about a person is stored, so the 30-day presence rule holds by design; the live state goes at archiving;
the counts stay with the event as anonymous statistics until it is deleted. Message counts and the top chatters are not ported (Q D6).
